title: How does offstage route a GUI command locally, and run cloud work on fleet Macs?
audience: Engineers onboarding to offstage and offstage cloud
scope: Local lane routing (headless, container, session, refuse); cloud tasks, sandboxes, computer-use agent runs and GitHub Actions jobs on fleet slots
omissions: Billing (Stripe), mail (Resend/SES), metering and admin routes are left out
site/, launch/, bench/ and tests/chaos are left out: not on the runtime path
Container lane internals and slot seeding/login (RFB) were not traced in detail

edges.label: A1 classify argv → lane, or refuse
A2 spawn in place → exit code, output
A2 docker run under Xvfb → exit, files
B2 submit: quota check → queued or 429
B3 claim: fair pick, bind box+slot
File: JSON snapshot every 2s; logs, artifacts
B6 fleet reset: recreate slot account
C2 ops long-poll ≤25s → op; POST answer
D3 HTTPS Messages API, customer's key
E3 Actions runner: run job, report results
HTTPS: verify session token, fetch user

notes.title: Two places decide where work runs
notes.text: Locally, classify() picks headless, container or session, and any refusing signal (installer, .dmg/.pkg, hdiutil) beats all three. In the cloud, boxes pull work: the queue hands the fairest team's task to a slot whose offer covers its session (headless or gui).

notes.title: State lives in memory, snapshotted to /data
notes.text: Accounts, keys, ledger, tasks, sandboxes and boxes are in memory and written to DATA_FILE every 2 s when changed, and on SIGINT/SIGTERM; a failed write is only logged. Ended task logs go to the archive. One Fly machine with a /data mount.

notes.title: Failure, isolation and retry
notes.text: A claim not started within CLAIM_ACK_MS (20 s) is requeued, up to MAX_ATTEMPTS (3), then fails never-started. A box unheard for BOX_LOST_MS (2 min) loses its work. A dirty slot is reset before its next claim, with backoff on failure. Lanes never fall back to the real screen.

views.title: Who calls the plane, and where does cloud work run?
views.scope: Customer clients and agents call the plane; the fleet box pulls work and runs it in slot accounts

notes.title: Pull model, no inbound ports
notes.text: Boxes only make outbound calls. A client's request is held open on the plane until a box claims the work, runs it and answers.

views.title: How does a local command get routed away from the real screen?
views.scope: Workflow A: offstage run/route through the classifier to the headless, container or session lane, or a refusal

notes.title: Refuse beats route
notes.text: A refusing signal returns refuse and nothing runs. The session lane checks the daemon's socket and uid; when a check fails it never falls back to the console.

views.title: How does a submitted task reach a slot and return its result?
views.scope: Workflow B: submit, queue, claim long-poll, execute in the slot, report events and artifacts

notes.title: Fair, acked claims
notes.text: A claim binds the task to box+slot. The box must report started within CLAIM_ACK_MS (20 s) or the task is requeued, up to 3 attempts.

views.title: What persists, and how is a slot cleaned between customers?
views.scope: Plane snapshot/archive and the per-slot reset after work

notes.title: Reset before the next claim
notes.text: A slot that ran work is marked dirty and reset before it claims again. A failed reset keeps the mark and is retried with backoff.

views.title: How do sandbox ops and computer-use agent runs execute?
views.scope: Workflows C/D: sandbox ops held open on the plane; a gui agent in the slot calls the model through the plane's proxy

notes.title: The agent loop stays in the slot
notes.text: The customer's Anthropic key arrives in a header on D1 and stays on the plane; the slot's agent calls the proxy with a run token only.

views.title: How do console sign-in and GitHub Actions jobs reach the fleet?
views.scope: Console auth through Clerk; workflow E: webhook → JIT runner config → job in a slot

notes.title: Clerk is checked server-side
notes.text: The plane verifies each Clerk session token against api.clerk.com; an unreachable Clerk gives 502, a bad token 401. Runners use per-job JIT configs.
